newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no trade-private.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no trade-private.

text.p: The Nebraska feedlot cattle market was quiet near midday on Monday, with no reported sales, market sources said.
Packers were bidding $104 to $105 per cwt, dressed, while owners were pricing cattle at $107.
The bulk of trade last week was at $104 although there was some trade last Thursday at $105.
"I would be very surprised if we see any trade today. They (packers) bought a lot of cattle last week," one source said.
USDA reported 83,700 head traded in Nebraska last week.
Cattle on a live basis were priced at $66 and $67.
There were no bids reported on a live basis.
